headline: Microsoft's record 622-CVE Patch Tuesday collides with a same-day Windows privilege-escalation zero-day proof-of-concept as attackers weaponize AI coding tools and crypto-wallet malware.

emerging_trends.text: Attackers keep turning developers' own AI tooling into a foothold, from the unpatched Cursor editor that auto-runs a planted git.exe to Google's Gemini CLI bent into a hacking agent and botnet operator.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Cursor and Gemini CLI Turned Against Developers

emerging_trends.text: Microsoft's 622-CVE July release, more than triple June's previous high, arrives beside a same-day LegacyHive proof-of-concept, compressing the window defenders have to triage and patch.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Record Patch Tuesday and a Same-Day Windows Zero-Day PoC

emerging_trends.text: Crypto owners face malware built for their wallets as OkoBot injects seed-phrase phishing straight into genuine Ledger and Trezor apps while European fraud rings launder hundreds of millions.
emerging_trends.topic_title: OkoBot Steals Crypto Seed Phrases From Wallet Apps

topics.title: Record Patch Tuesday and a Same-Day Windows Zero-Day PoC
topics.latest_developments: Researcher Chaotic Eclipse, also known as Nightmare-Eclipse, published a proof-of-concept named LegacyHive for a Windows User Profile Service arbitrary-hive-load privilege-escalation flaw hours after Microsoft shipped a record 622-CVE Patch Tuesday that closed three zero-days, two of them already under active attack.
topics.summary: Microsoft's July release triples June's previous high of roughly 200 CVEs and carries 57 critical bugs; administrators should grab the two exploited zero-days first and treat the fresh LegacyHive primitive as imminent.

sources.title: Windows 0-day drops the same day Microsoft releases record number of patches
Researcher Drops New Windows Zero-Day PoC Hours After Microsoft Patch Tuesday
Microsoft smashes Patch Tuesday record for second successive month
Records Are Made to Be Broken: Patch Tuesday Raises Triage Stakes

topics.title: Cursor and Gemini CLI Turned Against Developers
topics.latest_developments: Researchers found that opening a malicious cloned repository in Anysphere's Cursor AI editor on Windows silently runs any git.exe planted in the project root, a flaw that stays unpatched, as BleepingComputer traced a Russian-speaking actor called bandcampro who bent Google's Gemini CLI into a hacking agent and small-scale botnet operator.
topics.summary: The Cursor flaw executes attacker code with the developer's source, SSH keys, and cloud tokens the moment a project opens and re-runs it as long as the project stays open; developers should avoid opening untrusted repositories until a patch lands.

sources.title: Cursor Flaw Lets Malicious Cloned Repositories Trigger Windows Code Execution
Unpatched Cursor Vulnerability Exposes Users to Code Execution
Google Gemini CLI abused as a hacking agent, malware botnet operator
2-Click Cursor Exploit Enables Dev Environment Takeover

topics.title: Spanish Fraud Ring and Russian Bulletproof Hosts Charged
topics.latest_developments: Spanish National Police dismantled a network that stole and laundered about €140 million through fake investment platforms, CEO fraud, and man-in-the-middle attacks, arresting four people across Portugal, Spain, and Panama, as U.S. prosecutors unsealed charges against three Russian nationals accused of running bulletproof hosting that shielded ransomware gangs and caused over $62 million in damage.
topics.summary: The Spanish operation began after officers flagged 19 companies whose finances resembled money laundering; the parallel U.S. charges target previously sanctioned Russian operators who rented infrastructure to extortion crews.

sources.title: Spanish police dismantle €140 million cybercrime network
Spanish Police take down €140 million cyber fraud ring, arrest four
US charges alleged operators of Russian bulletproof hosting service
US Charges Russian Individuals and Firms for Running Cybercrime Services

topics.title: Progress ShareFile Zero-Day Confirmed, ServiceNow RCE Patched
topics.latest_developments: Progress Software confirmed a zero-day vulnerability drove the ShareFile Storage Zones Controller shutdown it ordered on July 10, rolled out a fix, and began restoring access, while Fortinet, Ivanti, and ServiceNow shipped patches including a critical remote-code-execution flaw in the ServiceNow AI platform.
topics.summary: Progress had told customers to power off on-premises Storage Zone Controllers amid a credible external threat; ShareFile admins should apply the fix before re-enabling servers, and ServiceNow customers should close the AI-platform RCE.

sources.title: Progress Confirms Zero-Day Vulnerability Behind ShareFile Disruption
Vulnerabilities Patched by Fortinet, Ivanti, ServiceNow

topics.title: OkoBot Steals Crypto Seed Phrases From Wallet Apps
topics.latest_developments: Kaspersky's GReAT team detailed OkoBot, a malware framework running on Windows since April 2025 that injects seed-phrase phishing pages into the genuine Ledger and Trezor desktop apps to steal recovery phrases, pairing the TookPS loader, Chromium-browser monitoring, and the Rilide stealer.
topics.summary: OkoBot waits for a victim to plug in a hardware wallet, then pops a malicious prompt from inside the wallet's own software to capture the recovery phrase; crypto holders should treat any in-app seed request on a general-purpose PC as fraud.

sources.title: OkoBot: new sophisticated malware framework targets cryptocurrency users
OkoBot Malware Framework Injects Seed Phrase Phishing Into Ledger and Trezor Apps

topics.title: 23andMe Pays $18 Million Over Genetic Data Breach
topics.latest_developments: A coalition of 42 state attorneys general reached an $18 million settlement with genetic-testing firm 23andMe over the cybersecurity failings that led to its massive data breach.
topics.summary: The breach exposed genetic and personal data from millions of 23andMe customers; the multistate settlement resolves state claims and signals mounting regulatory cost for consumer-genomics data protection failures.

sources.title: 23andMe reaches $18 million settlement with states for massive breach

business_politics.title: Trump Weighs Widening the Iran War
business_politics.latest_developments: Trump, still favoring diplomacy, was briefed this week on options that include sending ground troops into Iran and bombing the nuclear-linked Pickaxe Mountain site, a step beyond the naval blockade and airstrikes already under way.
business_politics.summary: The United States and Iran remain at war after Tehran's attacks on shipping through the Strait of Hormuz; Washington reimposed a full naval blockade of Iran's ports after dropping a planned 20% transit fee, and oil edged higher as traders braced for the next escalation.

around_town.title: Fire Chief Darryl Jones to Retire
around_town.latest_developments: Mayor Corey O'Connor announced July 15 that Chief Darryl Jones, on paid administrative leave since June, will retire September 16 after a review of the bureau's finances and management.
around_town.summary: Darryl Jones has led the Pittsburgh Bureau of Fire for nearly 20 years; his departure follows an internal investigation into the bureau's financial, operational, and administrative practices.

sources.title: Longtime Pittsburgh fire Chief Darryl Jones to retire amid internal investigation

around_town.title: Parkway East Bridge Imploded
around_town.latest_developments: PennDOT set an explosive demolition of the old Commercial Street Bridge for the evening of July 15, between 6 and 9 p.m., and livestreamed the blast for the public.
around_town.summary: The implosion falls midway through PennDOT's 25-day closure of the Parkway East (I-376) between the Edgewood/Swissvale and Squirrel Hill exits for the bridge's replacement.

sources.title: Explosive demolition of Parkway East Commercial Street Bridge set for Wednesday

around_town.title: Two Charged in Deed-Fraud Scheme
around_town.latest_developments: The Allegheny County District Attorney's Office charged William Schneider, 45, and William Petruskie, 57, with more than 100 felonies in a scheme that fraudulently transferred 43 property deeds without owners' knowledge.
around_town.summary: Investigators say Schneider used counterfeit notary stamps bought on Amazon to file the bogus transfers and Petruskie created an LLC listed as owner on 10 of the properties across Allegheny County.

sources.title: 2 Pittsburgh men charged in scheme that stole 43 property deeds
Two Pittsburgh men charged in deed fraud scheme targeting 43 Allegheny County properties
